our_interpretation: This is a qualified paraphrase of Altman's February roadmap, not a prediction of what OpenAI would eventually release.
In context, the combination of products means an integrated system incorporating o3 and other capabilities.
The preceding paragraph specifies standalone o3. I therefore read the access claim as withdrawal of the standalone release plan, not removal of o3 capability from GPT-5.
Mediocre is an evaluative judgment. The roadmap can establish the proposed packaging, not product quality.
Won't be a model at all is treated as rhetorical shorthand for system-level integration, not a literal claim that GPT-5 would contain no trained models.
criteria.support_condition: Altman's contemporaneous roadmap describes GPT-5 as an integrated system including o3 and says o3 will no longer ship as a standalone model.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The roadmap does not propose the stated integration, or retains the standalone o3 release plan.
